messages:
anya: Heads-up — after yesterday's RBAC tighten in prod, I'm seeing a small spike in cross-region mTLS handshake failures for egress proxies in eu-west -> ap-south. Errors in the audit logs look like KMS Decrypt Deny for cert-key unwraps. Anyone else seeing this? :thinking:
omar: saw a couple of alerts, didn't dig in yet. Can you paste a sample log line?
devops-jen: sec-bot posted an alert at 3991234605 about a failed unwrap against arn:aws:kms:ap-south-1:123456:key/abc-...
anya: here — 3991234598 root: "kms:Decrypt Denied" proxy=egress-proxy-3 region=ap-south-1 svc=ingress-relay dest=10.2.14.8:443 principal=svc-frontend-eu sub=svc-frontend-eu@redwood.internal tls_peer="CN=svc-ingest-ap,OU=redwood"
ryan: hm can we confirm whether the RBAC roles used by the proxy service account were narrowed in the recent PR? I remember we removed iam:Decrypt for a few edge roles.
lina: PR #4786 removed kms:Decrypt from role/edge-proxy-readonly in eu-west for least-privilege. That was part of the cross-region hardening work. I annotated a migration note but maybe we missed the egress-relay use-case.
anya: thought egress proxies used a dedicated role that was left intact, but logs show principal=svc-frontend-eu which is a tenant-facing pod — could be using the tighter role.
sec-bot: [ALERT] 3991234610 — correlated KMS:DecryptDenied events (count=24) from ap-south-1, affected service=svc-frontend-eu, suggested runbook=kb/kms-decrypt-deny.
omar: quick triage idea: are we picking up the wrong key alias in ap-south because of cert-issuer-affinity? If the proxy asks KMS to unwrap with a key from eu-west and the role lacks decrypt in ap-south, that will deny. Can we show the key id from the logs?
devops-jen: log snippet shows key_id=arn:aws:kms:eu-west-1:123456:key/abc-... but call was from ap-south host. That smells like a cert provisioning race where the cert manager cached issuer metadata from eu-west.
ryan: possible. Also remember we tightened ALPN/curves in envoy config; fallback to TLS1.2 was disabled in the rollout — if the handshake fails we might be cashing out to a flow that triggers different cert path selection. Not 100% sure though.
anya: action items to validate: 1) confirm which IAM role principal used for the KMS Unwrap call (node vs pod role). 2) check cert-manager issuer affinity logs and key alias resolution. 3) check whether the recent RBAC PR removed decrypt from any role associated with svc-frontend-eu.
lina: I can check PR audit and join a short call. I also have the RBAC diff: we removed kms:Decrypt from role edge-proxy-readonly and role svc-readonly-eu, but left role/egress-proxy-unified as-is. Might be that some pods are accidentally bound to svc-readonly-eu due to a label selector overlap.
omar: label selector bug would explain intermittent, cross-region-only failures. I've seen similar where the deployment template used legacy label key.
devops-jen: deploys team confirms a canary rolled out with new selector two days ago to eu-west, but a separate rollout to eu-central didn't include the label fix. Could be a split in how pods get bound to the updated role.
ryan: for immediate mitigation, can we add a temporary allow kms:Decrypt for the svc-readonly-eu role scoped to the specific key ARN in ap-south until we fix the selector? This buys time but we need an audit trail.
anya: I'm OK with scoped temporary allow if we document and set a 24h TTL. Need approval from security lead.
line: (typo) lina: pinging @ryan for approval, and I'll file a policy change with expiration.
ryan: approved for 24h scoped exception limited to key arn:aws:kms:ap-south-1:123456:key/abc-... and only for principal role/svc-readonly-eu. Post fix, we revoke. :thumbsup:
sec-bot: [AUDIT NOTE] 3991234660 — Temporary policy exception created by ryan; id=tmp-exc-3991234660; expires=3991235020. Logged in audit index.
anya: next, we need to harden cert provisioning: ensure cert-manager chooses region-local key alias and that issuer affinity is enforced. Also add telemetry to surface cross-region unwraps.
omar: quick grep suggestion for the cert-manager log: look for "selected key_alias" and "issuer_region". If we see eu-west chosen while running in ap-south that's the bug.
devops-jen: I'll add a transient metric: cert_unwrap_region_mismatch{host_region,selected_key_region} and put an alert if count>5/min.
lina: I'll audit role bindings for label selector overlap and push a fix to the deployment template.
anya: final ask — can oncall run the KMS audit query: "events where api=Decrypt and sourceRegion!=requestRegion and principal contains svc-frontend" for the last 6h and paste top 5 lines here? That'll confirm scope.
omar: on it, running now.
sec-bot: [QUERY] 3991234685 — results attached (5 rows):
- ts=3991234550 principal=svc-frontend-eu key=arn:aws:kms:eu-west-1:123456:key/abc... src_region=ap-south-1
- ts=3991234562 principal=svc-frontend-eu key=arn:aws:kms:eu-west-1:123456:key/abc... src_region=ap-south-1
- ts=3991234578 principal=svc-frontend-eu key=arn:aws:kms:eu-west-1:123456:key/abc... src_region=ap-south-1
anya: confirms it. Looks like selected key region != source region. That explains decrypt denies after RBAC tighten.
ryan: long-term fixes: 1) enforce key-region affinity in cert-manager and runtime, 2) add audit rule to flag cross-region unwraps, 3) tighten label selectors in rolebindings, 4) add unit tests for role-binding logic.
devops-jen: also let's document the mitigation steps in the incident runbook: how to create temporary scoped KMS allow, how to query audit logs, and how to roll back the RBAC change if needed. I'll create the PR and link kb/incidents/mtls-crossregion-2026.
anya: thanks all — prioritize the label fix + cert-manager guard. I'll follow up after lina's role-binding patch and once the temporary exception expires we'll verify no more denies. :white_check_mark:
